assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA or RNA molecules electrically as they thread a nanopore is a clean physical principle (ionic-current blockade) turned into a general analytical capability. It is original, quantitatively demanding and has opened long-read sequencing and single-molecule sensing. It sits at the physics-chemistry-biology border and can be explained to a broad audience.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton conceived and pursued polynucleotide translocation through nanopores; Kasianowicz, Brandin, Branton and Deamer gave the 1996 alpha-hemolysin demonstration; Bayley engineered pores; Akeson showed enzyme-controlled ratcheting that made sequencing practical. Deamer, Branton and Akeson span conception through to a working method. The Bayley and Kasianowicz roles are a real allocation issue, and I am not certain of the current status of every credited person.
assessment.maturity: Mature: commercial nanopore sequencers have been used for over a decade, with independent confirmation, genome-scale and field applications, and steady accuracy gains. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether Branton, Bayley or others can still be recognised, which I cannot verify.
Fair split of credit between the initial concept, pore engineering and enzyme-motor sequencing.
Part of the impact is in sequencing and genomics, which a chemistry citation must frame carefully.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took photovoltaic efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent within about a decade, a striking case of a new materials class approaching the limits of established technologies. The ideas about defect tolerance and carrier physics also have broad conceptual value.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell in 2009; Park delivered the first solid-state, durable cell in 2012; Snaith showed the meso-superstructured and planar thin-film routes. Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also made important contributions, so a three-person limit leaves out credible names.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are independently reproduced worldwide, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and scale-up are not settled. Recognition now is defensible, though commercialisation could make it more convincing later.
uncertainties: Operational stability and manufacturability remain open.
Contested credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis.
The discovery is a chain of steps and a single three-person citation may be too narrow.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami made it possible to build arbitrary nanoscale shapes from a programmable base-pairing principle, with a strong link between design, thermodynamics and kinetics. It supplies a general platform for nanofabrication, single-molecule physics and molecular machines, which suits the committee's interest in new capabilities.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 origami paper is the clear decisive step; Winfree's algorithmic self-assembly and Yin and Shih's later 3D and brick architectures extended it. Seeman's foundational work is not among the credited names, which complicates the story.
assessment.maturity: The method is widely reproduced and has produced well-established structures. Practical applications such as drug delivery and nano-devices are still emerging, so the impact is mainly in method and capability.
uncertainties: Seeman's foundational contribution is not on the list.
Applications are less proven than the structural method.
Relative weight of Rothemund, Winfree, Yan, Yin and Shih.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle in cells recasts how biochemistry is compartmentalised, and it is a physical-chemistry idea with a quantitative basis. It has reshaped cell biology and drug-discovery thinking.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman's 2009 P-granule work is the key discovery; Rosen's multivalent-interaction work provided the quantitative framework; Pappu and Mittag supplied sequence-grammar and theory. A fair set seems feasible, but Pappu and Mittag are close.
assessment.maturity: The field is very young and moving fast. Debate continues over physiological relevance, how general condensates are, and how they differ from artefacts of overexpression, so I see some risk of premature recognition.
uncertainties: Physiological relevance of many reported condensates is disputed.
Whether this is chemistry or cell biology in the eyes of the Academy.
Credit among five or more leaders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Using bifunctional molecules and molecular glues to direct proteins to the proteasome opens a genuinely new therapeutic modality, targeting proteins once thought undruggable. The chemistry is original and the generative potential is large.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies produced the first PROTACs; Ciulli made the VHL ligands and structure-guided design; Handa, Ito and others explained how thalidomide acts through cereblon. The split between PROTACs and molecular glues is a real attribution difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials of degraders are advancing but no PROTAC drug is yet approved to my knowledge. Confirmation is strong in the laboratory, while clinical validation is incomplete.
uncertainties: Clinical outcomes are pending.
Compound discovery: PROTACs and cereblon glues may need separate recognition.
Eight credited names make a clean three-way split hard.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography uses X-ray free-electron laser pulses to outrun radiation damage, giving structures from microcrystals and time-resolved views of reactions. The physical principle is elegant and the capability, diffraction before destruction, is new.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu and Chapman provided the diffraction-before-destruction concept and the first demonstrations; Fromme and Schlichting contributed key biological and time-resolved applications. The collaborative origin makes allocation delicate.
assessment.maturity: The method is confirmed at several facilities, although access is limited and many major results remain method demonstrations. Impact on chemistry is growing but narrower than the broadest candidates.
uncertainties: Dependence on a few large facilities limits its reach.
Whether time-resolved chemistry results are yet decisive.
Attribution among Chapman, Hajdu, Fromme and Schlichting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base to another at a target site without double-strand breaks, an original piece of chemical engineering that is already used in therapy research. It is a strong example of chemistry opening unforeseen capabilities.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab devised both cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead authors; Nishida and Kondo independently reported a related cytidine deaminase fusion. Liu is clearly central, and the others are a reasonable fit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is broad and clinical studies have started, with early patient data encouraging. Off-target effects and delivery remain active concerns. It is mature enough but the long-term record is short.
uncertainties: Overlap with prime editing, which may be recognised with it.
Genome-editing prizes may be viewed as medicine rather than chemistry.
Independent Nishida and Kondo credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Preserving noncovalent assemblies in the gas phase lets mass spectrometry measure stoichiometry, subunit connectivity and ligand binding of intact complexes, including membrane proteins. It is a decisive analytical advance with lasting uses in structural biology.
assessment.attribution: Chait, Robinson and Heck are the most plausible principal contributors, with Loo and Gross also relevant. The credited set is larger than a prize can hold, which makes credit hard to allocate.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed, widely used and still developing, though most of the field's impact is complementary to cryo-EM and crystallography. It already has a long record, so timing is not premature.
uncertainties: Competition with other structural methods lowers perceived impact.
Allocation among at least five credible names.
Precursor ESI-MS work already recognised in 2002 may lead some members to see this as incremental.
